chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: Goodman and classical music; musicians who cross over
summary: Goodman is happiest in jazz; Previn crossed, Mel Powell did not.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yes, but other people have speculated likewise.
But he plays so well, really. Maybe he shouldn't try classical, although he loves it. He's not so successful at that.
He's probably bothered that he used to be, after he studied with Kall Cat.

I think it's deeper than that. Jazz is his thing. The other he loves and there is no doubt that he loves it, he doesn't do it for prestige. That may be there, but I don't think that's the main reason. I think if he really didn't love it, he wouldn't do it. It does something for him, but he doesn't have the heritage training of that sort of thing, the sort of thing that you must do when you're very young.
I think it's like anything else. You have to be totally immersed.
The only one I know that has made that crossing is the conductor, --
Yes, I suppose, but even he got to a point where he had to make a decision to concentrate on the classical.
Oh, yes, but he has made the crossing. He became a good conductor.
I don't know, his jazz might have suffered, but the point is he made that crossing.
I don't think Mel has been a successful writer.
I've never heard any of his concert music.
